segments.content:
Chapter 102 0099: Publishers Fight Over Him (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Leader Fa Wen Baobao)

Publishing houses also close for the National Day holiday.

Shencheng.

Chunfeng Literature and Art Publishing House.

Shi Xiang, a senior editor in charge of youth literature, had come back to the office during the holiday to unwind.

He was in a very good mood.

"Shi Ge, Vice President Chang wants to see you."

"Coming."

Beaming, Shi Xiang headed for Vice President Chang Jing's office.

"Knock, knock, knock."

The door was open, so Shi Xiang gave it a few symbolic knocks, then walked straight in after a two-second pause.

Vice President Chang said, "We failed to secure Guo Xiaosi's new book. 21st Century Publishing House snatched it."

"How could that be?" Shi Xiang was stunned.

He was Guo Xiaosi's true benefactor!

Back then, no one had high hopes for *Huan Cheng*. Even the publisher of *The Edge of Love and Pain* thought the novel had no future.

It was Shi Xiang who, in the dead of winter, took a train from Shencheng to Shanghai to discuss with Guo Xiaosi how to publish and market *Huan Cheng*. Immediately after, Shi Xiang also helped with the publication and marketing of *How Many Flowers Fall in a Dream*.

Shi Xiang was also the one handling Guo Xiaosi's *Island* series.

Shi Xiang had always believed that no matter what book Guo Xiaosi published, he would choose to work with him.

Vice President Chang sighed. "21st Century Publishing House has gone mad. *The Happy Times Carved Down* is just a photo-essay collection, yet they were willing to offer the royalty rate of a full-length novel! That Guo Xiaosi will go with whoever pays more. For a tiny bit of extra royalty, he kicked us to the curb."

Shi Xiang grumbled inwardly: I told you not to suppress Guo Xiaosi's royalties. If he can make more money elsewhere, why would he stick with us?

Although Guo Xiaosi was mired in a plagiarism scandal, in the eyes of publishing houses, he was still a hot commodity.

The news that he planned to release a photo-essay collection purely to cash in immediately drew a frantic scramble from multiple publishers.

Li Xunhuan's (the future exclusive publisher for Han Han, Director Lu) move was the most brilliant. He planned to simultaneously market Guo Xiaosi's new book and the second edition of Zhuang Yu's *In and Out of the Circle*.

In other words, bind the plagiarist and the plagiarized together for publication!

Li Xunhuan had even managed to persuade the plagiarized party. As long as the plagiarist added a line in the new edition saying, "Thank you to Zhuang Yu's novel for the inspiration," the two could shake hands and make peace, not even needing to continue the lawsuit.

Everyone makes money together, a joyous occasion for all.

However, Guo Xiaosi refused...

Li Xunhuan was left speechless and turned to seek a partnership with Han Han instead.

"Will Guo Xiaosi's *Island* still be a collaboration with us?" Shi Xiang asked.

Vice President Chang said, "The company has decided to cut it off. Does he think we're pushovers?"

Shi Xiang hesitated. "But aren't there still two issues left?"

"Cut it off!"

"He's not the only celebrity to come out of the New Concept Writing Competition," Vice President Chang tossed a copy of *Sprout* over. "Chen Guiliang has a very positive image. The man got into Peking University on his own merit. He already started serializing a full-length novel during the National Day holiday."

Shi Xiang took the copy of *Sprout*, found Chen Guiliang's novel using the table of contents, and frowned after reading for a few minutes. "Isn't this just translating the *History of Ming* into humorous, modern language? It'll be a miracle if it sells a hundred thousand copies."

"Not necessarily. The response to the serialization has been excellent," Vice President Chang said.

Shi Xiang asked, "Should I make a trip to Peking University then?"

Vice President Chang said, "Go get in touch with him."

In Tongliao, the center of the universe, the future nine-year-old Khan was chortling as he read *Sprout*.

"Have you finished your National Day homework?" the Old Khatun asked.

The little Khan said, "Mom, I finished it a long time ago."

"What extracurricular book are you reading now?"

"It's *Sprout*. My sister next door was reading it, so I'm just flipping through. I'm studying history, really. Look if you don't believe me."

"This is history?"

"It's about the Ming Dynasty. It's hilarious."

The Old Khatun snatched the copy of *Sprout*. She had only meant to check it, but she ended up getting engrossed in it herself.

There was absolutely no barrier to entry for reading; it was suitable for men, women, young, and old.

It didn't matter if you disliked history; you could just read it as a humorous story.

The little Khan stood beside her, his eyes filled with longing.

The Old Khatun chuckled as she read the twenty-thousand-plus-word installment for 50 minutes, then casually tossed it back to her son. "Here, you can have it."

The little Khan received it like a precious treasure.

"Senior, the issue of *Sprout* I bought has been passed all around our class."

Tao Xue said excitedly over the phone, "Everyone loves your *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*. They say they can learn history effortlessly. Even the students who don't usually like reading *Sprout* are really into your serialized articles."

Chen Guiliang laughed. "It's all thanks to your help with publicity."

Tao Xue said, "I also went on the Sprout forum and saw a lot of people discussing it. They all say your writing is incredibly interesting."

"I bet there are also people who can't stand me, cursing me for translating history books to cheat manuscript fees?" Chen Guiliang said.

Tao Xue said, "Those are just a tiny few. I've already replied and scolded them. A lot of netizens joined me in scolding them, and we flamed those few until they didn't dare to show their faces."

Chen Guiliang broke into a cold sweat.

He actually had fans fighting battles for him now.

After chatting for a while, Tao Xue asked, "Are you coming home for winter break this year?"

"We just finished the National Day holiday," Chen Guiliang said.

"Alright then."

"Listen well in class, study hard. I'll be waiting for you at Peking University."

"It's a deal. I'm going to do my homework now. Senior... Hmph, goodbye, big nephew!"

"Goodbye, Auntie Xue."

After hanging up, Chen Guiliang lay down in his dorm to rest.

Over the past few days of the National Day holiday, Chen Guiliang had ridden his bicycle to visit nearly all the surrounding universities.

One reason was to hang out with Bian Guanyue.

The other was to familiarize himself with the major universities, which would be convenient for promoting *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* and Xiaonei Network in the future.

Bian Guanyue was overjoyed, sitting on the back of the bicycle every day, admiring the scenery of different university campuses.

After a few days, her kissing skills had improved considerably.

He hadn't been lying down for long when the phone rang again.

"Hello, may I ask if this is student Chen Guiliang?" the person on the other end asked.

"This is he."

"Hello, this is Wan Yu, an editor from Writers Publishing House. I'd like to talk to you about publishing *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*."

"I've only serialized just over twenty thousand words."

"Roughly how long do you plan for this book to be?"

"About a million words or so."

"How many?"

"About a million words."

"That's... not very convenient to publish. I suggest you release it in volumes."

"What royalty rate does your publishing house plan to offer?"

Chen Guiliang got up from his bed, sat down at his computer, and asked, "What are the royalty rates for Han Han and Guo Xiaosi?"

Wan Yu paused for a moment. "15%. Your book is different; it falls under the category of popular history science, and its sales will naturally be lower than their youth novels. Besides, Han Han and Guo Xiaosi didn't get 15% for their first books either. Fame is linked to royalty rates. You need a book to make a name for yourself first. For a new author with some fame, 8% is already very high. Yu Hua's royalty rate is only 12%."

"Let me think about it. You can also discuss it further among yourselves," Chen Guiliang said.

Wan Yu said, "Alright, we'll discuss it some more."

That afternoon, Chen Guiliang received calls from several publishing houses one after another.

His new phone number was likely spread by Hu Weishi.

One publisher was the stingiest, offering a royalty rate of only 6%. They were treating Chen Guiliang like a complete newcomer, completely ignoring his fame among high school students.

If a complete newcomer published a work, how could it attract so many publishers?

Right now, the major publishing houses in China were especially fond of snatching up writers who emerged from the New Concept competition, willing to publish even extremely daunting works of pure literature.

The next day, evening.

Chen Guiliang received another call.

"Hello, this is Chen Guiliang."

"Hello, I'm Shi Xiang from Chunfeng Literature and Art. I was the one who marketed *Huan Cheng* and *How Many Flowers Fall in a Dream*."

"Editor Shi, you have a great eye," Chen Guiliang chuckled.

Shi Xiang said, "I'm almost at Peking University. Do you have time to meet?"

"Sure. Let's meet at Sage Cafe in All Sages Bookstore, near the East Gate of Peking University. When can you get here?"

"Within half an hour. I'm on the subway right now. Please bring the rest of your manuscript with you as well."

Teachers and students from the many nearby universities loved to browse All Sages Bookstore. The old man standing by the bookshelf could very well be some renowned professor.
